prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a foreground wooden table surface about 0.4–1.0 m directly in front of and below the camera wearer, a seated person across the table at roughly 1.0–1.3 m in the center, a curved dirt path and grass at 3–10 m behind the person, and a tree line over 15–30 m away in the upper background. In frame 1, the orange cup on the lower left (~0.5 m) and the blue water bottle and objects on the right (~0.7–0.9 m, about 0.5 m right of the cup) protrude above the table within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the seated person, while the table occludes the person's lower body. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera pitches upward and slightly left, causing the table and tabletop objects to drop almost entirely out of the bottom of the frame (leaving only a bright sliver of the right table edge in frames 2–5) and cropping the person below the shoulders while their distance remains steady. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the backlit, shadowed silhouette of the seated person and the dark blue water bottle (including its thin loop handle) from the dark background trees and table shadow. However, the map is unreliable in its relative depth scaling across frames—as the very close table leaves the view after frame 1, re-normalization makes the person and background trees appear brighter in frames 2–5 despite no actual forward approach, and smaller flat items like the dice, paper, pen, and phone are merged into the table surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the seated person in the center-foreground (~1.0–1.3 m away), the wooden table surface below them (~0.4–1.0 m away), and the orange container on the lower left (~0.5 m away, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person), while leaving the background path, grass, and trees unlabelled in black. In frame 1, the person is positioned directly behind the table surface (which occludes their waist and legs) and roughly 0.4 m behind and to the right of the labelled cup, facing toward the camera wearer with their head tilted downward toward the tabletop. From frame 1 to frame 5, as the camera tilts upward, the segmented person shifts to the bottom center of the frame and is progressively cropped at the chest and shoulders, while the table and cup move completely below the lower frame boundary after frame 1. This map makes it easier than in the high-contrast RGB image to see the exact outer contour of the heavily shadowed person against the dark foliage, as well as the distinct footprint of the cup on the left. However, the segmentation is unreliable in several places: it misclassifies the wooden picnic table as a 'boat' in frame 1, creates unlabelled black cutouts on the right side of the table where the water bottle, hat, phone, and pouch sit, and fails to detect the visible bottom-right corner of the table in frames 2–5 or any of the dice and stationery.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map tracks the upper-body keypoints of the single person seated about 1.0–1.3 m directly in front of the camera wearer, showing their torso facing forward toward the camera and their head angled downward toward the table surface below. In frame 1, both shoulders, elbows, wrists, and hips are visible above and behind the occluding tabletop, with the person's right arm bent upward so the right wrist rests near the chin and the left arm resting downward within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) of the tabletop objects (dice, paper, pen, and water bottle on the right). In frame 2, as the camera pitches upward, the person shifts toward the bottom edge so the hips and left arm drop out of view, leaving only the head keypoints, shoulder line, and raised right arm visible. In frames 3 through 5, the map is completely black and fails to detect the person at all because the camera tilt crops their body below the upper chest, leaving too little of the torso in view for the pose estimator. While frames 1 and 2 clearly reveal the bent right-arm posture and downward facial orientation (eye, ear, and nose keypoints) that are obscured by deep shadow in the RGB frames, the map is unreliable due to a horizontal hip-line artifact extending to the left in frame 1, the complete absence of magenta hand skeletons in all frames, and total detection failure in frames 3–5.
